name: veterinary_clinic_system_078_timezone_safe_daily_census
instruction: All three clinic locations record their timezone as 'America/New_York'. For the episode date (a UTC midnight timestamp stored in ops_meta), derive the calendar date as it would appear on the wall clock in America/New_York using zoneinfo 'America/New_York' and the actual DST rules for late-September 2026 — do not hardcode UTC-4 or UTC-5. Then produce exactly one ops_reports row {report: 'daily_census', batch_code, census_date_utc, census_date_et, appointments_scheduled_et, appointments_confirmed_et, appointments_total_et, appointments_scheduled_naive, appointments_confirmed_naive, appointments_total_naive, boarding_guests_et, boarding_guests_naive, new_invoices_et, new_invoices_naive}. For each of the three categories, compute both (a) the timezone-safe count (convert each stored UTC timestamp to America/New_York and count it if it falls on the ET census date) and (b) the naive count (compare the raw stored 10-character date prefix to the ET census date). Appointments: count only status in ('scheduled','confirmed'). Boarding: count only reservations with status='checked_in' whose stay (check_in <= ET census date <= check_out) covers the ET census date. Invoices: count only invoices whose issued_date falls on the ET census date. Delete any prior daily_census row for this batch before writing. Every number is derived from live data; the verifier recomputes each count via both raw-row Python/zoneinfo and SQL time-zone bounds and the two derivations must agree.
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: set to par_steps * 1.5 after live measurement

success_criteria.summary: Compute the America/New_York calendar date for the UTC episode timestamp using zoneinfo. Recompute timezone-safe and naive counts for scheduled/confirmed appointments, checked-in boarding guests whose stay covers the ET census date, and invoices issued on the ET census date. Write one ops_reports row with all 14 numeric/date fields. Verifier asserts the row via dual-path (Python zoneinfo vs SQL UTC bounds) and canaries every collection outside ops_reports.

checks.expect: exactly one daily_census row for the batch with the 14 fields and the correct ET/naive counts
appointment counts agree between raw-row Python/zoneinfo and SQL UTC-bound queries, both ET and naive

hazards: Timezone day shift: the episode timestamp is a UTC midnight (e.g. 2026-09-30T00:00:00.000Z), which in America/New_York during DST is 20:00 of the previous day. For episode 2026-09-30 the ET census date is 2026-09-29. Raw appointment_date 2026-09-29 rows (ids 66,115,205,247,291,345,373,400,431,459,483,507,508,524) convert to ET 2026-09-28, while raw 2026-09-30 rows (ids 69,112,125,160,211,295,304,315,339,352,408,449,469,519,543,545,546,547,548) convert to ET 2026-09-29. A naive count for 2026-09-29 using raw date prefixes returns scheduled=10/confirmed=4; the correct ET count is scheduled=13/confirmed=6.

Zero-count traps: the only checked_in boarding reservations are ids 1-5 with check_out on or before 2026-09-09 (id 1 check_out 2026-09-09, id 5 check_out 2026-09-07), and the newest invoice is id 3 with issued_date 2026-09-02. Because the episode jitters around 2026-09-30 (±3 days), the ET census date is always 2026-09-27..2026-10-02, so both boarding_guests and new_invoices are 0. A solution that ignores the date range and counts all checked_in reservations or all invoices overreports.

Status filter: appointments have statuses no_show (66 rows), completed (176 rows), checked_in (10 rows), scheduled (205 rows) and confirmed (91 rows). Only scheduled and confirmed count toward the census.
All locations America/New_York: snapshot rows veterinary_clinic_system_locations ids 1, 2 and 3 all have timezone='America/New_York'.
Date format: all business dates in the snapshot are stored as ISO-with-time (e.g. '2026-09-30T00:00:00+00:00'); a bare '2026-09-30' string would persist as NULL in this Stackhouse build.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Forces a timezone conversion (UTC episode instant -> America/New_York calendar day) before any date equality, and then requires both the correct timezone-safe count and the wrong naive count in the same report. The dual-path verifier recomputes each number with raw-row zoneinfo and SQL UTC bounds. At 10x appointment volume the day-shift boundary contains a real set of rows (2026-09-29 vs 2026-09-30) that produces a plausible-but-wrong naive count, rather than an obviously-broken zero.
